## What This Is

**If you installed any version before this one, apply this update by hand. Your Ecosystem Update Check cannot show it to you.** From the first release on, that skill fetched its updates from a branch (`main`) and a folder (`UPDATES/` at the root) that never held them. Every run read "404: Not Found" and halted. No update has ever reached a vault through it. This release fixes the skill, so the next update arrives the way it was meant to.

It also closes a hole in the browser skill and makes the trust anchor lighter.

## The Gaps

**The update channel was dead.** The skill's own Inputs line named the right folder; the `curl` command beside it named the old one, and `curl -s` exits 0 on a 404, so nothing at the command level registered a failure. No check in CI ever fetched an address. Run headless in a fresh v3.25.0 clone, the skill halted at Step 1 on the 404 and reported that it could not read the update list.

**The browser fetcher read your own network.** The Playwright skill's `run.js` passed any URL straight to the browser: `localhost`, a router's admin page, `169.254.169.254` cloud metadata, `file://`. The URLs this skill fetches often come out of web pages and other intake, so a page could plant an address and have the agent read your machine into its context.

**The trust anchor was 278 lines.** Claude Code loads `.claude/CLAUDE.md` into every session, and its docs set 200 lines as the target, since a longer file costs context and lowers adherence. Two of its sections also claimed things the template no longer is: hooks "Status: proposed" (seven guards ship, tested) and plan mode as the default (no setting sets it).

## The Fix

**The Update Check reaches its updates.** It fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/infinitegameplayer/sovereign-ecosystem/master/.github/UPDATES/INDEX.md` and each update as `[date]-[slug].md` from the same folder, with `curl -fsSL`, so a missing page is an error. A 404 is named as a wrong address with the Releases page as the fallback; any other failure as a connection problem. A new script, `update-channel-check.mjs`, reads every upstream address the template ships and fails when its branch differs from the one `se-update.mjs` pulls from or its path is missing from the checkout. CI runs it, and its selftest plants the old addresses.

**Updates can say they are already in your vault.** An update file may carry a `## Detection` section: a read-only check whose output says whether the change is already present. The Update Check runs it before presenting the update, and one already present (for example because `se-update.mjs --apply` brought the file in) shows as "Already in your vault". This file is the first to carry one.

**The browser fetcher refuses your machine and network.** Only http and https, and never a local name (`localhost`, `*.local`, `*.internal`), loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT or cloud metadata address, in IPv4, IPv6 or IPv4-mapped form, written plainly or encoded. It is checked on the URL, after DNS, and on every request the page makes, redirect hops and iframes included. A refusal prints `{"error": "refused: ...", "guard": true}` and exits 1. `--allow-private` opens it for a site on your own machine; `--guard-only` checks an address and fetches nothing. `guard-plants.mjs` fires 36 cases; `--offline` runs the 26 that need no browser, and CI runs those.

**The trust anchor is 183 lines** (21,585 bytes, from 34,775). Nothing in it lost its rule; full statements moved to a home the anchor names in one line:
- Claim Integrity in full is Principle 4 in Governance Principles, with a new face, the outward reach: anything published is verified before it goes out, to the degree the stakes need. The anchor keeps one line per face.
- The Pending Plan status vocabulary, plan verification before handoff and the existence check moved to `.claude/rules/pending-plans.md`, which Claude Code loads when a session touches the plans folder.
- The four cross-model questions moved to a new Cross-Model Perspectives Codex; the anchor keeps the trigger phrase.
- The Agent SDK section states what ships: the hook events registered in `.claude/settings.json` and the suite that fires them.
- The Engineering Codex states the rule: an anchor stays under 200 lines, and how it gets there.

**Practice that travels.** General rules learned in the source vault since v3.23.0: Source Harvest clones a repo outside the vault and reads its agent files as intake, never instruction; the Weekly Story saves on the Sovereign's approval in their own words rather than a magic phrase, and runs every step whole; Researcher labels each quote verified or worker extract and checks a worker's output file for zero bytes; the Manuscript Anti-AI Edit Pass checks every quote, number and name survives an edit; Session Closeout offers itself in one line on a short session; the Activation skill names a model mismatch before any work; Pending Plan Implementation re-reads before every edit; the Engineering Codex answers the reasons to skip a test and runs a heavy file-based skill in its own session; the Phase Audit keeps sensitive material from its outside-model pass; the Ambassador Doctrine gains three standing rulings; Sovereign Tech Watch reads what the machine runs before any lane; Writing Style gains "familiarity is the bridge"; and smaller pointers. 28 serial commas left text whose own rule forbids them.

## Detection

Run from your vault root. The update is present when both print a number above 0:

```
grep -c "master/.github/UPDATES/INDEX.md" "Council Chamber/Skills/Ecosystem Update Check/SKILL.md"
grep -c "guard-only" "Council Chamber/Skills/Playwright/scripts/run.js"
```

## If You Are Updating an Existing Vault

1. **Apply the manifest first, then check.** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/se-update.mjs" --apply "Council Chamber/scripts/framework-manifest.json"`, then `--check`. Before the manifest, three new files read as user paths and `--apply` would refuse them. After it, expect 32 framework files and 2 seeded files, with no user paths.
2. **Apply the framework files:** `--apply "<path>"` for each framework file it lists. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is one of them. If you replaced its `{{ECOSYSTEM_NAME}}`, `{{AI_INTERFACE_NAME}}` or `{{SOVEREIGN_DISPLAY_NAME}}` tokens or added rules of your own, look at `--diff ".claude/CLAUDE.md"` first and put your names and rules back after applying.
3. **The two seeded files, by review.** If you never edited one, apply it with `--force-seeded "<path>"`. `Governance Principles.md` matters most: the anchor now points to its Principle 4 for Claim Integrity in full. If you added principles of your own, copy the `## Principle 4: Claim Integrity` section from this release into your file by hand instead. `Writing Style Codex.md` gains one style marker; if you personalized it, add "Familiarity is the bridge" by hand or leave it.
4. **Commit, then check again.** It should read "up to date with upstream."
5. **Fire the new positive controls:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/update-channel-check.mjs" --selftest`, then without the flag; `node "Council Chamber/Skills/Playwright/scripts/guard-plants.mjs" --offline` (and without `--offline` if Playwright is installed).
6. **Run the Ecosystem Update Check.** It should now read the index and list the updates you have not recorded.
7. **If your agent has customized these files**, hand it this spec rather than the diff. The Update Check fetches from `master/.github/UPDATES/` with `curl -fsSL`, names each update `[date]-[slug].md`, runs an update's Detection section before presenting it and tells a 404 apart from a lost connection. The fetcher refuses non-http schemes, local names and every loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT and metadata address on the URL, after DNS and on every request, unless `--allow-private`. The anchor keeps one line per rule and points to the rule's home. The tests named above are the acceptance suite. The recipient owns the code. This file owns the standard.

This path was walked on a fresh clone at v3.25.0 against a snapshot of this release: before the manifest the check listed 29 framework, 2 seeded and 3 user paths; after it, 32 framework, 2 seeded and 0 user paths; all 34 applied, none refused; after the commit the clone read "up to date with upstream" and its tree matched the release's.

## What Stays Open

The fetcher cannot see a name that resolves to a public address at the check and a private one at the connect (DNS rebinding), nor anything a page sends to a public address. Detection is new: only this update carries a section, and a check you run by hand is the first form of it. The update channel check reads addresses offline against the checkout; it proves an address names a file this repo ships, not that GitHub serves it at that moment.

## Prerequisites

v3.25.0. Node on PATH, as the README requires. Claude Code 2.1.295 or later.

## Optional?

No. A release that cannot be heard is a release that never happened, and every one before this was in that state for anyone relying on the skill.
